findings.title: Singleton selection windows falsely commit rejected callbacks
findings.reproduction: Open prompt_editor, action_picker, or model_browser with a callback that returns false or raises, then deliver the matching live bridge save, confirm, or select message; the current window closes although the requested mutation did not commit.
findings.root_cause: The bridge marks or closes its singleton session before invoking the controller and discards both protected-call status and explicit false refusal.
findings.silent_failure: Bare pcall deletes callback exceptions, callback false is ignored, and existing tests cover stale contexts but not operational refusal.
findings.regression_test: Drive each real bridge and prove false or exception keeps the same context open and retryable, success closes once, re-entrant delivery invokes at most once, and exceptions reach the logger.

findings.title: Deferred MLX boot cleanup still blocks the Hammerspoon run loop
findings.reproduction: Fire init.lua's zero-delay cleanup timer while the cleanup command reaches curl --max-time 1 or the sleep 0.3 nuke branch; no Hammerspoon callback can run until hs.execute returns.
findings.root_cause: run_selective_cleanup uses synchronous hs.execute and init.lua mistakes hs.timer.doAfter(0) for an off-run-loop execution boundary.
findings.silent_failure: A source meta-test pins doAfter(0) and falsely asserts it prevents blocking, while the headless suite stubs hs.execute to return immediately.
findings.regression_test: Prove cleanup uses a retained asynchronous task, never hs.execute, reports start/completion failures, and gates backend bootstrap on terminal cleanup settlement.

findings.title: Download terminal action runs AppleScript synchronously
findings.reproduction: Post the terminal message to the real download-window bridge with a slow osascript process; the bridge and Hammerspoon run loop remain blocked until the child exits.
findings.root_cause: The live WebView callback calls hs.execute inline to launch osascript instead of using the asynchronous shell adapter.
findings.silent_failure: The interactive blocking ratchet scans shortcut and gesture directories but omits this WebView action, and tests stub hs.execute as immediate.
findings.regression_test: Drive the real bridge and prove it dispatches the exact AppleScript asynchronously, reports launch or completion failure, and never calls hs.execute.

findings.title: Input-source notifications synchronously spawn defaults
findings.reproduction: Start the input-source watcher, hold hs.execute inside the installed broker callback, and fire a layout notification; the callback cannot return or debounce the rebuild until the process exits.
findings.root_cause: The notification path calls read_current_layout_from_hitoolbox synchronously even though the same module owns a generation-fenced asynchronous defaults reader for polling.
findings.silent_failure: Tests cover the asynchronous poll but not the primary notification path, and the source comment explicitly accepts the synchronous call as infrequent.
findings.regression_test: Exercise notification and poll through one asynchronous single-owner read transaction with watchdog, generation fencing, visible acquisition failure, and no hs.execute call from the notification.

findings.title: WebView controller callbacks delete exceptions
findings.reproduction: Install a throwing cancel, resolve, retry, preference, focus, or config-refresh controller and deliver its real bridge or close event; the controller runs but no central error is emitted.
findings.root_cause: Download and hotstring WebView modules call external controllers through bare pcall and never inspect or log the failure.
findings.silent_failure: The exception is contained by pcall, so the headless bridge continues and the UI click appears successful while the file logger receives nothing.
findings.regression_test: Drive the real bridge and lifecycle callbacks with throwing controllers; prove exactly-once invocation, containment, and contextual ERROR logging.

findings.title: Gesture frame failures are silently discarded
findings.reproduction: Register a throwing any-touch hook and process a non-empty frame, or make a completed gesture action throw; the action is lost and state resets without a file-log error.
findings.root_cause: The frame processor wraps both the external touch hook and commitGesture in unchecked pcall calls.
findings.silent_failure: Containment makes the callback look successful, while resetGS removes the remaining observable state and no log identifies the dropped gesture.
findings.regression_test: Prove both paths contain exceptions, log the first contextual error, throttle repeated frame-hook failures, and preserve safe gesture-state reset.

findings.title: Keylogger listener failures silently stale live dashboards
findings.reproduction: Register one throwing and one successful ingest listener, then complete ingest_once; both are called but the first dashboard misses the new revision without any ERROR.
findings.root_cause: The log manager explicitly invokes ingest listeners and shutdown completion callbacks through unchecked pcall calls.
findings.silent_failure: Listener isolation keeps later callbacks and the ingest cycle green, but the thrown dashboard update is deleted and repeated ticks provide no diagnostic.
findings.regression_test: Prove throwing listeners do not stop siblings, their first failure is logged with stable context, repeats are throttled, and shutdown callbacks use the visible boundary.
